name: manual_504ae3
claim: An unconflicted git auto-merge is not proof a local fix survived it -- git can silently resolve a hunk in favor of the 'wrong' side (reverting a prior local patch back to its pre-fix state) without ever flagging a conflict, if the two sides' diffs don't textually overlap in a way git's 3-way merge detects. After any merge that touches files with a known local-patch history (e.g. an .agentic-stack-blend-state.json applied_clean list), diff the post-merge content against the expected patched content directly -- don't trust 'no conflict markers' as proof the fix is still there.

decisions.notes: 9 of 16 files with UTF-8/context-manager fixes mined from the agentic-stack v0.18 blend-preview got silently reverted by 'git merge origin/main' during PR #206 reconciliation -- none were flagged as conflicting, so the revert went unnoticed until an explicit post-push content verification (grep for bare open() calls) caught it. Re-applied and re-committed; updated .agentic-stack-blend-state.json's own record to note this exact gotcha for future blend cycles.
